outline:
國際合作專題特論乃透過國際大師的講課，讓學生學習材料科學或資源工程相關領域的重要知識及了解最先進之研究成果或最新開發成品。
This course will provide important information regarding to the latest development or application in the materials science and mineral engineering. Speakers being invited are well-known international scholars in the related area.

Electromagnetic Material Interactions: Theory and Practice

Alternating electric fields and microwave interactions with materials are of interest for diverse areas including energy storage, telecommunications and magnetic resonance imaging. The course is intended for students that have an interest in electromagnetic interactions with matter. Students with backgrounds in bioengineering, neuroscience, chemistry, food science, electrical engineering, engineering science and mechanics, and materials are invited to enroll in this interdisciplinary course. In addition to lectures, students will have hands-on laboratory and simulation experiences.

Fundamental dielectric, magnetic, and conduction properties of materials will be explored and how these properties influence electromagnetic field interactions with a variety of substances will be discussed. The course will introduce the fundamentals of dielectric measurement and electromagnetic modeling and highlight links between electromagnetic field analysis and device design. The level will be targeted to non-EM specialists who would like to learn more about the roles of dielectric and magnetic properties on device performance. In addition, capacitors, microwave devices, the fundamentals of magnetic resonance imaging, as well as artificially engineered materials, i.e. metamaterials will be explored. The course will also cover electrostatic energy storage, microwave heating and processing, which involves polymers, ceramics, metals, composite, food products and biological systems.
